MIDLAND, Texas--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- ProPetro Holding Corp. (“ProPetro” or “the Company”) (NYSE: PUMP) today announced financial and operational results for the third quarter of 2026.


**Third Quarter 2026 Results and Highlights**


- Total revenue of $355 million, which increased 16% as compared to $306 million for the prior quarter.
- Net income was $13 million ($0.09 income per diluted share) as compared to a net loss of $8 million in the prior quarter ($0.07 loss per diluted share).
- Adjusted EBITDA(1) of $60 million was 17% of revenue and increased 33% as compared to the prior quarter.
- Capital expenditures paid were $123 million and capital expenditures incurred were $171 million.
- Net cash provided by operating activities and net cash used in investing activities were $46 million and $122 million, respectively.


**Recent PROPWR** ® **Highlights**


- Generated approximately $8 million of Adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter, a meaningful sequential increase, driven by deployment execution and reliability that continue to exceed expectations.
- Power generation capacity committed under contract reached approximately 510 megawatts, including approximately 230 megawatts under the recently announced Targa agreement.
- Continued to advance negotiations across several hundred megawatts of data center commercial opportunities, with discussions strengthened by the Company's proven track record as one of the few behind-the-meter power providers actively servicing a hyperscaler data center project.
- Expect to deploy more than 500 megawatts by early 2028 fueled by scaling currently contracted projects and beginning to scale one or more additional data center projects.


*(1)*


*Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP financial measure and is described and reconciled to net income (loss) in the table under “Non-GAAP Financial Measures.”*


**Management Comments**


Sam Sledge, Chief Executive Officer, commented, “ProPetro delivered a solid third quarter, with continued progress in PROPWR and higher revenue and activity across our completions service lines. We are pleased to have generated a meaningful step-up in earnings in PROPWR as we continue to advance its commercial and operational execution coupled with improved revenue and Adjusted EBITDA from our completions business.


“PROPWR continues to build on its success as we scale through year-end and advance deployment efforts across our contracted portfolio, which includes awards in the data center, oil and gas, midstream and industrial sectors. These deployments are also strengthening our commercial efforts by showing prospective customers our execution and reliability firsthand. As we move into 2027, we expect to continue executing across our projects, including one or more additional data center customers, and to have more than 500 megawatts deployed by early 2028.


“Demand for our completion services remains strong and continues to build, consistent with what we have seen over the past few quarters. While the cost of rebuilding the business’s capacity after declining activity levels in 2024 and 2025 has weighed on margins, improved pricing and better visibility into the duration of work have supported recent reactivations, and our capacity is now essentially sold out. Years of attrition have drastically reduced the supply of high-quality horsepower, and with our estimate that active Permian frac fleets are only in the mid-70s today, even a modest increase in drilling activity, particularly from larger public and independent operators, would fully tighten the market. Regardless of how the conflict in the Middle East unfolds, we expect demand for natural gas-burning fleets, which make up the majority of our fleet, to remain especially strong, as limited supply and global refining constraints keep diesel prices elevated and sustain the premium these fleets already command. As the majority of our contracted horsepower comes up for renewal in the first half of 2027, we believe the more constructive pricing environment provides an opportunity to begin realizing returns on our investment in reactivating capacity, which we expect could support improved results in the completions business over time.


“ProPetro’s track record speaks for itself. We continue to execute across the business, and our results show the strength of our strategy: a strong completions business, paired with a premium growth platform in PROPWR that keeps delivering commercially and operationally with each new deployment. Together with a strong balance sheet, thoughtful capital allocation and a world-class team, we are confident in our ability to create long-term value for our shareholders.”


**Third Quarter 2026 Financial Summary**


Revenue was $355 million, compared to $306 million for the second quarter of 2026. The 16% increase in revenue was primarily driven by higher revenues from increased utilization in the completions business and incremental deployments in PROPWR.


Cost of services for the third quarter of 2026 were $270 million, excluding approximately $42 million of depreciation and amortization expenses.


General and administrative (“G&A”) expense of $31 million decreased from $33 million in the second quarter of 2026. G&A expense excluding nonrecurring and noncash items of $5 million (stock-based compensation, business acquisition contingent consideration adjustments, retention bonuses and severance expenses) was $26 million, or 7% of revenue, a decrease of 4% as compared to the prior quarter.


Net income totaled $13 million, or $0.09 income per diluted share, compared to a net loss of $8 million, or $0.07 loss per diluted share, for the second quarter of 2026.


Adjusted EBITDA increased to $60 million from $45 million in the second quarter of 2026, primarily driven by higher revenues from increased utilization in the completions business and incremental deployments in PROPWR, partially offset by higher costs associated with rebuilding the operational infrastructure needed to support increased completions activity.


Net cash provided by operating activities was $46 million as compared to $66 million in the prior quarter. The decrease is primarily attributable to working capital headwinds in the third quarter, which consumed approximately $15 million of cash and working capital tailwinds in the prior quarter, which were an approximately $20 million source of cash, partially offset by higher Adjusted EBITDA.


**Liquidity and Capital Spending**


As of September 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents were $729 million, including net proceeds from the issuance of $690 million aggregate principal amount of convertible senior notes. Borrowings under the Company's financing agreement with Caterpillar Financial Services Corporation were $172 million. Total liquidity at the end of the third quarter of 2026 was $934 million, which included cash and cash equivalents, $185 million of available borrowing capacity under the ABL Credit Facility, and $20 million of availability under its Caterpillar Equipment Loan Agreement. The Company currently has no outstanding borrowings under the ABL Credit Facility.


During the third quarter of 2026, capital expenditures paid were $123 million and capital expenditures incurred were $171 million, including approximately $43 million supporting the Company's completions business and approximately $128 million supporting its PROPWR equipment orders. Notably, the difference between incurred and paid capital expenditures is primarily comprised of PROPWR-related capital expenditures that have been financed and paid directly by the financing partner and unpaid capital expenditures included in accounts payable and accrued liabilities. Net cash used in investing activities as shown on the statement of cash flows during the third quarter of 2026 was $122 million, which included capital expenditures paid of $123 million, offset by $1 million in proceeds from certain asset sales.


**PROPWR Update**


Mr. Sledge commented, “Since our last update, we have made significant progress across the business. PROPWR generated approximately $8 million of Adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter, a meaningful sequential increase. Results and margin performance at the project level continue to meet our high expectations, which reinforces our confidence in the earnings and return profile we have outlined.


“We expect to keep scaling deployments through year-end, reaching between approximately 250 and 275 megawatts deployed by the end of 2026 and stair-stepping to more than 500 megawatts by early 2028. We expect this growth to come from three sources: scaling our currently contracted capacity, deploying or preparing to deploy on the Targa award, which is scheduled to be fully deployed by early 2028, and beginning to scale one or more additional data center projects over time.


“Commercially, our recently announced agreement with Targa for approximately 230 megawatts brings our total capacity committed under contract to approximately 510 megawatts. This award represents meaningful progress in our commercial efforts. It also shows how broad power demand is across end markets, including oil and gas, midstream and industrial, in addition to data centers. Contract terms in these sectors are generally shorter than those in the data center arena, but pricing and expected annual returns are very attractive. That said, given the larger load requirements and longer contract durations in the data center arena, along with the depth of our pipeline there, we continue to expect to deploy the majority of our assets to data center projects.


“Of the approximately 2.6 gigawatts of power generation capacity we have secured, more than 1 gigawatt consists of Caterpillar’s highly efficient 10-megawatt units, which are a part of our strategic framework agreement. With supply chains for power generation equipment remaining very tight, we believe this agreement and our early-mover position provide a meaningful advantage. Beyond securing supply, the 10-megawatt units themselves are highly efficient stationary natural gas engines purpose-built for permanent, high-density installations. They maximize efficiency for our customers while lowering our total cost of ownership. The vast majority of our fleet will be natural gas reciprocating engines ranging from 2 to 10 megawatts, which we believe are the ideal fit for every vertical we are pursuing. Of note, our smaller units are also proving to be successful: our first data center deployment to support a hyperscaler, which is live and operating today in the U.S. Midwest, is built largely on 2.6-megawatt units. Reciprocating engines offer a number of advantages that we believe make them the right fit for our customers. They are a proven technology with a long track record in both mechanical drive and power generation applications. They are continuous-duty rated machines trusted in high-availability environments, including data centers, oil and gas, mining and industrial operations, and marine and heavy transport, where uptime and performance are critical. They provide flexibility, scaling in modular blocks alongside customer demand with built-in redundancy. They deliver high fuel efficiency, are cost-effective for both PROPWR and our customers, and are emissions-friendly, which supports an efficient permitting path. These advantages apply across our entire fleet, with our 10-megawatt units adding even greater scale for our customers’ largest power needs.


“In the data center arena, despite broader volatility and noise in the AI market, we remain in advanced negotiations on several hundred megawatts and continue to progress a number of additional opportunities behind them. Our pipeline also continues to grow, strengthening our conviction in our strategy and investments. As we have noted previously, timelines have extended as we work through diligence with counterparties. These agreements involve long-term capital commitments on both sides, so getting the risk-sharing provisions right is critical. Strong demand for our assets can also lengthen, rather than shorten, the contracting process, because we are being deliberate about choosing the right long-term partners. In addition, a change in scope or timing on one project can make a previously unworkable opportunity viable, or free up capacity for customers we otherwise could not support. Because we are allocating capacity across multiple customers, individual deal timelines may shift as we determine how each opportunity fits within our broader portfolio. Accordingly, we feel very confident in this pipeline.


“Importantly, we are currently deployed and operating on a hyperscaler project, and execution has gone exceptionally well. We are one of the very few behind-the-meter power providers live on a data center site today, and we believe this operating track record validates our strategy and has helped accelerate our broader commercial efforts.”


**Guidance**


The Company anticipates full-year 2026 capital expenditures incurred to be between $525 million and $575 million. Of this, the completions business is still expected to account for approximately $125 million to $145 million, largely dependent on delivery timelines of certain capex related items heading through year end and into 2027. The Company continues to expect buyout costs for its first FORCE® electric fleet to be between $15 million and $20 million, with at least three additional buyouts occurring in 2027.


In addition, the Company anticipates incurring capital expenditures of approximately $400 million to $430 million for its PROPWR business in 2026, narrowed from prior guidance due to greater year-end visibility into the timing of additional equipment deliveries. Notably, the Company's previous guidance of approximately $1.4 million to $1.5 million per megawatt inclusive of balance of plant remains unchanged. While these PROPWR capital expenditure estimates reflect the total cost of the equipment, they do not reflect the impact of financing arrangements, which have and are expected to continue reducing the near-term actual cash outflows required from the Company. Looking ahead to 2027, PROPWR is aligning equipment delivery schedules under the Caterpillar framework agreement and remains in active discussions on data center opportunities, both of which could affect the timing and amount of capital expenditures for the year. In particular, the size, timing and structure of any new data center agreements could change when equipment is needed and how much balance of plant investment is required next year. However, the Company expects that any such changes would affect the timing and total amount of capital expenditures rather than the cost per megawatt, which it continues to expect to remain within the guided range. That said, the Company expects 2027 PROPWR capital expenditures to increase from 2026 levels, driven by the delivery of additional equipment and the funding of down payments and milestone payments under the Caterpillar framework agreement.


The Company currently expects to maintain steady activity of approximately 13 active frac fleets through the fourth quarter. That said, the Company expects meaningful seasonality in the completions business in the fourth quarter driven by typical holiday-related slowdowns toward year-end, which is expected to temporarily affect utilization and results for the quarter, along with continued margin pressure from rebuilding costs similar to those experienced in the second and third quarters. As activity stabilizes moving into 2027, the Company expects to begin optimizing those costs, although the full benefit will take time.


Looking ahead to 2027, PROPWR’s primary focus will be preparing for larger, infrastructure-scale projects, including the Targa award, which is expected to be fully deployed by early 2028, and potential additional data center awards, which could begin deploying as early as late 2027. As a result, the Company expects 2027 earnings to be weighted toward the latter part of the year, with growth following a stair-step pattern as projects come online rather than a straight line throughout the year. Projects of larger scale require significant lead time, and the Company expects certain costs, including personnel, site preparation and mobilization, to build ahead of these deployments before the corresponding revenue and earnings are realized. By emphasizing disciplined execution and actively de-risking these larger deployments, the Company is building on the strong operational foundation established in 2026, and it remains confident in its PROPWR guidance and the long-term earnings and return profile of the business.


Additionally, certain PROPWR contract structures may include reservation fees that are collected in cash up front but not recognized in revenue or Adjusted EBITDA until the assets are deployed and generating power. As a result, PROPWR’s revenue and Adjusted EBITDA in a given period may trail the levels implied by its contracted capacity and guidance, though the underlying contract economics remain intact.


**Outlook**


Mr. Sledge concluded, “As we look ahead to 2027, I want to briefly summarize how we see the opportunity across both of our businesses. In completions, the setup is straightforward: a sold-out fleet, a tightening market, and early pricing momentum. We still have work to do on the cost side as we absorb the elevated expense of standing the system back up, but as activity stabilizes, our focus shifts from rebuilding to optimizing, and we expect to bring those costs down over the course of 2027. In PROPWR, our primary focus remains commercial and operational execution: converting our pipeline into signed, long-term contracts, then deploying and operating those assets reliably for our customers. We’ve secured the equipment to support that growth, and our performance in the field is strengthening our commercial position as we advance additional data center opportunities. We expect 2027 to be a year of building toward larger, infrastructure-scale deployments, with growth weighted to the second half.


“Across both businesses, we are doing what we said we would do, and we are excited about the opportunity in front of us. The completions market is moving in our favor, PROPWR is executing and scaling, and we have the balance sheet, the equipment and the team to capture what is ahead.”

**About ProPetro**


ProPetro Holding Corp. is a Midland, Texas based provider of premium completion services to upstream oil and gas companies engaged in the exploration and production of North American unconventional oil and natural gas resources. Through its PROPWR division, ProPetro also delivers reliable, adaptable power services through a modern, standardized fleet of gas-to-power solutions, serving data center, oil and gas, and industrial customers in the United States. ProPetro helps bring reliable energy to the world, enabling operational excellence and energy reliability for their customers. For more information, visit[www.propetroservices.com](http://www.propetroservices.com/) .

**Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


*Adjusted EBITDA, Free Cash Flow and Free Cash Flow for Completions Business are not financial measures presented in accordance with GAAP. We define EBITDA as net income (loss) plus (i) interest expense, (ii) income tax expense (benefit) and (iii) depreciation and amortization. We define Adjusted EBITDA as EBITDA plus (i) loss (gain) on disposal of assets, (ii) stock-based compensation, (iii) business acquisition contingent consideration adjustments, (iv) other expense (income), (v) other unusual or nonrecurring (income) expenses such as impairment expenses, costs related to asset acquisitions, insurance recoveries, one-time professional fees and legal settlements and (vi) retention bonus and severance expense. We define Free Cash Flow as net cash provided by operating activities less net cash used in investing activities. We define Free Cash Flow for Completions Business as net cash provided by operating activities less net cash used in investing activities less net cash provided by operating activities for PROPWR or plus net cash used in operating activities for PROPWR plus net cash used in investing activities for PROPWR.*


*We believe that the presentation of these non-GAAP financial measures provide useful information to investors in assessing our financial condition and results of operations. Net income (loss) is the GAAP measure most directly comparable to Adjusted EBITDA, and net cash from operating activities is the GAAP measure most directly comparable to Free Cash Flow and Free Cash Flow for Completions Business. Non-GAAP financial measures should not be considered as alternatives to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures. Non-GAAP financial measures have important limitations as analytical tools because they exclude some, but not all, items that affect the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures. You should not consider Adjusted EBITDA, Free Cash Flow or Free Cash Flow for Completions Business in isolation or as a substitute for an analysis of our results as reported under GAAP. Because Adjusted EBITDA, Free Cash Flow and Free Cash Flow for Completions Business may be defined differently by other companies in our industry, our definitions of these non-GAAP financial measures may not be comparable to similarly titled measures of other companies, thereby diminishing their utility.*
